meta.title: May Asks the Tour Guide
meta.textType: functional: an interview, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by May. On Saturday, the Explorers visited the small zoo. We met a tour guide there. Today is Monday, March fifteenth. This is my interview with her. Leo's pen pal Ravi asked in an email, "What does a tour guide do?" This post is for Ravi and the pen-pal class. Teacher Kim read this post first, and then it went on the blog. Mia took a photo of the guide, and you can see it on this page.

First, I asked, "How long have you been a guide?" She says that she has worked at the zoo for twelve years. Next, I asked, "What was your first job?" She says that she was a waitress in a small restaurant. She liked her customers, but her career at the zoo began later. Then I asked, "Who is your boss?" She says that her boss is the zoo director. The director is the boss of all the zoo staff.

After that, I asked, "What are your working hours?" She says that she works from nine o'clock to five o'clock. I also asked about her journey to work. She says that she takes a bus from the bus station. The journey takes twenty minutes. Here is my small map of our town. The key shows the zoo, the bus station, the bridge, the library, and the post office. The dotted line is the bus route, so Ravi can see where the zoo is.

Then I asked, "What does a guide need?" She says that a guide needs three things, for example a good voice, a map, and a smile. She tells me that every member of the staff wears an identification card. She showed me her card. She wears it around her neck. New guides are taught about every animal in the zoo. I think that a guide needs to be kind, too, because many visitors ask the same question.

My last question was, "What is your favorite place?" She says that it is the gibbon house, because the gibbons sing in the morning. The gibbon house is popular with children, so it is often crowded. She tells me that a baby gibbon was born there last month. The birth was a big day for all the staff.

Here is my opinion: a guide has a good job, because every day is different. Are you interested in a job with animals, Ravi? Which job are you interested in? What would you ask a guide? Please write to us in the comments.
text.summary: May writes an interview with the zoo tour guide for the pen-pal class, because Ravi asked what a guide does. The guide tells about her jobs, her boss, her hours, and her favorite place, and May adds a map.
